extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, agency counsel, administrative law practitioners, and legislators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for U.S. federal administrative agencies on rulemaking, adjudication, hearings, recordkeeping, publication, enforcement, and judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act and attendant Attorney General commentary. Intended to guide agency behavior and evaluate whether agency action comports with required procedures and legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of person and party
rubrics_metrics.description: "Person" includes individuals, partnerships, corporations, associations, or public or private organizations of any character other than agencies. "Party" includes any person or agency named or admitted as a party, or properly seeking and entitled as of right to be admitted as a party, in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may admit a person or agency as a party for limited purposes; these definitions set who is covered by procedural protections in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of rule and rule making
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rule" means the whole or any part of any agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe the organization, procedure, or practice requirements of any agency... "Rule making" means agency process for the formulation, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes future-oriented approvals/prescriptions (rates, wages, prices, facilities, valuations, accounting) and is deliberately broad; Attorney General commentary stresses this differentiates prospective regulatory action (rulemaking) from retrospective adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of order and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Order" means the whole or any part of the final disposition ... of any agency in any matter other than rule making but including licensing. "Adjudication" means agency process for the formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudication generally refers to case-specific determinations (often accusatory in character); the Act classifies proceedings into rulemaking vs adjudication to tailor procedural safeguards appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of license and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: "License" includes ... any agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, membership, statutory exemption or other form of permission. "Licensing" includes agency process respecting the grant, renewal, denial, revocation, suspension ... or conditioning of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers full lifecycle of permission-type actions and triggers procedural protections for licensing actions under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sanction and relief
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sanction" includes prohibitions, requirements, limitations, withholding of relief, penalties, destruction/seizure of property, assessment of damages/fees, revocation/suspension of a license, or other compulsory/restrictive action. "Relief" includes grants of money, assistance, license, recognition of claims/rights, or other beneficial actions on application or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly defines agency coercive and beneficial actions; both are within the scope of "agency action" for publication and review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency proceeding and agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency proceeding" means any agency process as defined in subsections (c), (d), and (e). "Agency action" includes every agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, or the equivalent or denial thereof, or failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes scope of the Act's procedural and review provisions by capturing both action and inaction across rulemaking, adjudication, and licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of organization, procedures, and methods (Public Information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register descriptions of its central and field organization (including delegations of final authority and places/methods for public information/submissions); statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined including nature/requirements of formal/informal procedures and forms/instructions; and substantive rules and statements of general policy or interpretations formulated for public guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person may be required to resort to unpublished organization or procedure. Attorney General commentary: publication requirement supplements Federal Register Act; statements of policy published only when formulated with sufficient definiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of opinions, orders, and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall publish or make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in adjudications (except those confidential for good cause and not to be cited as precedents) and all rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential material may be kept but should not be cited as precedent; agencies may provide abstracts of confidential material showing relied-upon principles without revealing facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of public records
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters of official record shall, in accordance with published rule, be made available to persons properly and directly concerned, except information held confidential for good cause found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not intended to open all government files generally; agencies should classify material by confidentiality and publish rules identifying confidential categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register and shall include (1) statement of the time, place, and nature of public rule making proceedings; (2) reference to the authority under which the rule is proposed; and (3) either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception when all persons subject are named and personally served or have actual notice; interpretative rules, statements of policy, rules of agency organization/procedure/practice, or where agency finds good cause may be excepted. Attorney General commentary: the "terms or substance" requirement may be satisfied by a description of issues if that is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to participate in rulemaking (procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: After required notice the agency shall afford interested persons opportunity to participate in rulemaking through submission of written data, views, or arguments with or without opportunity to present orally; after consideration of all relevant matter presented, the agency shall incorporate in any adopted rules a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statute requires rulemaking on the record after a hearing, sections 7 and 8 procedures apply instead. Attorney General: concise statement need not be an elaborate analysis but should provide the public a general idea of purpose and basic justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates of substantive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication or service of any substantive rule shall be made not less than thirty days prior to its effective date, except for rules granting/recognizing exemptions or interpretative rules/statements of policy, or upon a published finding of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must publish a finding of good cause when earlier effective date is necessary; the notice of good cause should accompany the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition for rule issuance, amendment, or repeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall accord any interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms public access to request regulatory changes; agencies should have published procedures to accept and respond to petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of adjudicatory hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing shall be timely informed of (1) the time, place, and nature thereof; (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held; and (3) the matters of fact and law asserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties who are moving private persons must give prompt notice of issues contested; agencies may require responsive pleadings; scheduling must consider convenience and necessity of parties or representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present facts, arguments, and settlement offers in adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall afford all interested parties opportunity for (1) submission and consideration of facts, arguments, offers of settlement, or proposals of adjustment where time/nature/public interest permit; and (2) where controversy cannot be resolved by consent, hearing and decision upon notice and conforming with sections 7 and 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties can attempt settlement or present full case; when statutory requirement exists for on-the-record hearings, adhere to sections 7 and 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions and prohibition of ex parte contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers who preside at reception of evidence shall make the recommended or initial decision except where unavailable. Such officers shall not consult any person or party on any fact in issue unless upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate; they shall not be subject to supervision/direction by investigative or prosecuting officers; and investigative/prosecuting personnel shall not participate in decision-making of factually related cases except as witness or counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects impartiality of adjudicators; exceptions apply for initial license determinations or specified utility proceedings and does not apply to agency members as bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to issue declaratory orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is authorized in its sound discretion to issue a declaratory order to terminate a controversy or remove uncertainty, with like effect as other orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies flexibility to resolve disputes outside of full adjudication when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel and representation (Appearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear in person before an agency shall have the right to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel or, if permitted by the agency, by other qualified representative. Every party shall have right to appear in person or by counsel or duly qualified representative in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not create or deny the right for non-lawyers to represent others; agencies must proceed with reasonable dispatch while considering convenience of parties/representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on investigative process and rights to copies
rubrics_metrics.description: No process, requirement of a report, inspection, or other investigative act or demand shall be issued or enforced except as authorized by law. Every person compelled to submit data or evidence is entitled to retain or procure a copy/transcript on payment of lawfully prescribed costs, except in nonpublic investigatory proceedings where inspection may be limited for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards against unlawful investigative demands and preserves a party's right to records of what they provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena issuance and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency subpoenas authorized by law shall be issued to any party upon request and, as may be required by agency rules, upon a statement/showing of general relevance and reasonable scope. Upon contest, courts shall sustain subpoenas found in accordance with law and, in enforcement proceedings, may order compliance under penalty of contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow published rules for issuing subpoenas; courts can enforce subpoenas subject to legal standards of relevance and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notice and explanation of denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt notice shall be given of the denial in whole or in part of any written application, petition, or other request of any interested person made in connection with any agency proceeding. Except in affirming a prior denial or where self-explanatory, such notice shall be accompanied by a simple statement of procedural or other grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures affected persons receive timely actionable information about denials and the grounds for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officers and impartiality in hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officers at taking of evidence may be the agency, members thereof, or examiners appointed; their functions must be conducted impartially. Any such officer may withdraw if disqualified; agencies shall determine affidavit claims of bias as part of the record and decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officials must avoid bias and may be recused; agencies must address disqualification claims on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing powers of presiding officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers presiding at hearings shall have authority, subject to published agency rules, to (1) administer oaths, (2) issue subpoenas authorized by law, (3) rule upon offers of proof and receive relevant evidence, (4) take or cause depositions, (5) regulate the course of the hearing, (6) hold settlement/simplification conferences, (7) dispose of procedural requests, (8) make or recommend decisions in conformity with section 8, and (9) take other actions authorized by agency rule consistent with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the scope of procedural control hearing officers may exercise; must act within agency rules and statutory powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards in hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as statutes otherwise provide, the proponent of a rule or order shall have the burden of proof. Any oral or documentary evidence may be received, but agencies shall as a matter of policy provide for exclusion of irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence; no sanction or rule/order shall be imposed except upon consideration of the whole record or such portions cited and supported by reliable, probative, and substantial evidence. Parties have right to present evidence, rebuttal, and to conduct cross-examination necessary for full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances broad admissibility with agency duty to exclude wasteful or irrelevant matter; in rulemaking or claims for money/benefits or initial licenses, agencies may adopt written-evidence procedures where not prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record as exclusive basis for decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcript of testimony and exhibits, together with all papers and requests filed in the proceeding, shall constitute the exclusive record for decision in accordance with section 8 and, upon payment, made available to the parties. If agency decision rests on official notice of material fact not appearing in the evidence, any party shall on timely request be afforded opportunity to show the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits decision-making to the administrative record and provides an opportunity to contest extra-record facts relied upon by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and agency decisions; review of subordinate decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where officers other than the agency preside, such officers shall initially decide the case or the agency shall require the record certified for initial decision. Initial decisions become agency decisions unless appealed or reviewed in time. On appeal or agency review, the agency has all powers it would have in making the initial decision, except as it may limit issues by notice or rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits delegation of fact-finding but preserves agency authority to review and decide; agencies may set rules for certification and for limiting scope of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to submit proposed findings, conclusions, and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to each recommended, initial, tentative, or agency review decision, parties shall be afforded reasonable opportunity to submit (1) proposed findings and conclusions, (2) exceptions to decisions or recommended decisions or tentative agency decisions, and (3) supporting reasons for such exceptions or proposed findings or conclusions. The record shall show rulings upon each such item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties a chance to shape the agency's written findings; agencies must record their disposition of each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of agency decisions (findings and reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions (including initial, recommended, or tentative decisions) shall be part of the record and include a statement of (1) findings and conclusions, as well as the reasons or basis therefor, upon all material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented on the record; and (2) the appropriate rule, order, sanction, relief, or denial thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates reasoned decisions that disclose the agency's basis on material issues, supporting review and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional and statutory authorization for sanctions and orders
rubrics_metrics.description: No sanction shall be imposed or substantive rule or order be issued except within jurisdiction delegated to the agency and as authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits agency power to what statute authorizes; acts beyond statutory jurisdiction are subject to invalidation on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: License proceedings: notice, opportunity, and protection against summary revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is made for a license required by law, the agency, with due regard to rights of interested parties, shall set and complete required proceedings under sections 7 and 8 and make its decision with reasonable dispatch. Except in willfulness or where public health/safety requires otherwise, no withdrawal/suspension/revocation/annulment of any license shall be lawful unless facts or conduct warranting such action were called to licensee's attention in writing and licensee accorded opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance with lawful requirements. Timely and sufficient renewal applications prevent expiration until final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects licensees from summary deprivation without notice and an opportunity to respond; allows exceptions for willful conduct or urgent public safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person suffering legal wrong because of any agency action, or adversely affected or aggrieved by such action within the meaning of any relevant statute, shall be entitled to judicial review thereof, except where statutes preclude review or agency action is by law committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves broad availability of courts to review agency actions subject to statutory exceptions; scope of review described in subsequent provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and venue for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of proceeding for judicial review shall be any special statutory review proceeding relevant to the subject matter in any court specified by statute or, in absence/inadequacy thereof, any applicable form of legal action (including declaratory judgments or writs) in any court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexibility in selecting procedural vehicle and forum for review when statute does not prescribe a single exclusive route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewable acts and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency action made reviewable by statute and every final agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in any court shall be subject to judicial review. Preliminary/procedural/intermediate agency actions not directly reviewable shall be subject to review upon review of the final agency action. Agency action otherwise final shall be final for purposes of this subsection whether or not reconsideration has been presented/determined unless agency by rule provides inoperative interim effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which actions are subject to judicial scrutiny and preserves review of final agency determinations even if internal reconsideration exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim relief authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending judicial review any agency is authorized, where it finds that justice so requires, to postpone the effective date of any action taken by it. Every reviewing court authorized to review may issue necessary and appropriate process to postpone the effective date of any agency action or to preserve status or rights pending conclusion of review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both agencies and courts can grant interim measures to prevent irreparable injury while review is pending; courts may impose conditions to protect interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of judicial review (standards of invalidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing court shall decide all relevant questions of law, interpret constitutional and statutory provisions, and determine meaning/applicability of terms of any agency action. It shall (A) compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed; and (B) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be (1) arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law; (2) contrary to constitutional right/power/privilege/immunity; (3) in excess of statutory jurisdiction/authority/limitations, or short of statutory right; (4) without observance of procedure required by law; (5) unsupported by substantial evidence in cases subject to requirements of sections 7 and 8 or otherwise reviewed on the record of an agency hearing; or (6) unwarranted by the facts to the extent those facts are subject to trial de novo by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court reviews whole record or portions cited by parties and accounts for rule of prejudicial error; enumerates grounds by which courts may set aside agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment, duties, and protections for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall appoint as many qualified and competent examiners as necessary for proceedings under sections 7 and 8; examiners shall be assigned to cases in rotation so far as practicable and perform no duties inconsistent with examiner responsibilities. Examiners shall be removable by the agency only for good cause established and determined by the Civil Service Commission after opportunity for hearing and upon the record. Examiners shall receive compensation prescribed by the Commission independently of agency recommendations or ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to secure qualified, impartial hearing officers with protections against arbitrary removal; Civil Service Commission has oversight and rulemaking/enforcement powers regarding examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction, severability, and non-diminution of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Act shall be held to diminish constitutional rights or to limit or repeal additional requirements imposed by statute or otherwise recognized by law. All requirements or privileges relating to evidence or procedure shall apply equally to agencies and persons. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall not be affected. Agencies are granted all authority necessary to comply with the Act. Subsequent legislation shall not supersede or modify the provisions of the Act except expressly. Effective dates for sections are staggered as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms Act is procedural floor, not ceiling; includes severability and grants agencies authority to issue rules to comply; specifies effective dates (e.g., sections 7 & 8 effective six months after approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General interpretive guidance on classification of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are to be classified into rulemaking and adjudication: rulemaking covers regulations of general applicability and subject matter demanding technical judgments; adjudication covers case-specific disputes often with accusatory elements requiring safeguards on the facts as they appear on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary explains intent to avoid overly cumbersome procedures for rulemaking while ensuring adequate procedure for adjudication; cites examples differentiating prescribing future rates (rulemaking) from determining past lawfulness (adjudication).
